candidates.title: Pruning via Causal Attribution Preserves Reasoning Performance in Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) excel at multi-step reasoning but incur substantial inference cost. We introduce Causal Attribution Pruning (CAP), a training-free method that identifies critical attention heads by measuring their causal impact on reasoning tasks and uses these head-level scores to guide fine-grained weight pruning. For each attention head, CAP estimates the expected performance degradation when the head is masked during forward passes on a small calibration set of reasoning problems. These causal scores are then converted into weight-level importance values for the corresponding projection matrices. Unlike magnitude-only or activation-based criteria, CAP's interventional measurement directly captures each head's functional contribution, yielding relative accuracy gains of up to 61% over Wanda on ARC-Challenge at 20% sparsity. We evaluate CAP on GSM8K, StrategyQA, and ARC-Challenge using Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct at 10%, 20%, and 50% sparsity. At moderate sparsity (10-20%), CAP improves over Wanda in most model-benchmark configurations. with especially large gains on ARC-Challenge for Llama-3. Our results suggest that attention-head-level causal attribution can better preserve reasoning performance on downstream benchmarks than correlational pruning criteria at equivalent sparsity, while remaining limited by coarse MLP attribution at 50% sparsity.
candidates.reason: 推論コストの高いLLMに対し注意ヘッドの因果的寄与を測って学習なしで重みプルーニングするCAPは、推論向けモデル圧縮として直接の貢献がある。

candidates.title: Hardware Accelerator for Approximation-Based Softmax and Layer Normalization in Transformers
candidates.abstract: Transformer-based models have achieved remarkable success across various AI tasks, but their growing complexity has led to significant computational and memory demands. While most optimization efforts have focused on linear operations such as matrix multiplications, non-linear functions like Softmax and layer normalization (LayerNorm) are increasingly dominating inference latency, especially for long sequences and high-dimensional inputs. To address this emerging bottleneck, we present a hardware accelerator that jointly approximates these non-linear functions using piecewise linear approximation for the exponential in Softmax and Newton–Raphson iteration for the square root in LayerNorm. The proposed unified architecture dynamically switches operation modes while reusing hardware resources. The proposed accelerator was implemented on a Xilinx VU37P FPGA and evaluated with BERT and GPT-2 models. Experimental results demonstrate speedups of up to 7.6× for Softmax and 2.0× for LayerNorm, while maintaining less than 1% accuracy degradation on classification tasks with conservative approximation settings. However, generation tasks showed greater sensitivity to approximation, underscoring the need for task-specific tuning.
candidates.reason: Transformer推論で支配的になるSoftmaxとLayerNormを近似ハードウェアで共同加速しBERTとGPT-2で評価する設計であり、推論カーネル・演算器への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: GA-SVD: Generation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for LLM Compression
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong generalization across a broad range of reasoning and generation tasks, but their large parameter counts impose substantial memory and computation costs, hindering deployment in practical resource-constrained settings. One-shot low-rank compression is a promising solution since it reduces model size and inference cost effectively. However, existing SVD-based methods primarily target multiple-choice benchmarks and often fail to preserve performance on generation tasks. Moreover, their rank allocation strategies are typically heuristic. We propose GA-SVD, a generation-aware low-rank compression framework for LLMs. First, we introduce Generation-Aware Weight Whitening (GAWW), which leverages gradients from on-policy knowledge distillation to construct whitening transformations aligned with generative behavior. Second, we develop an evolutionary global rank allocation method that searches for effective layer-wise rank allocation under a given global compression ratio. Across extensive experiments on Mistral-7B, Qwen3 series, and Llama-3.3 models, evaluated on both multiple-choice and generative benchmarks, GA-SVD consistently outperforms existing SVD-based baselines and achieves state-of-the-art (SoTA) results. We further demonstrate scalability by applying our method to models with up to 70B parameters.
candidates.reason: 生成時の活性を意識した特異値分解でLLMをワンショット低ランク圧縮するGA-SVDは、資源制約下のLLM配備・推論メモリ削減へ直接寄与する圧縮手法である。

candidates.title: SGA-Sparse: Training Native SwiGLU Gates for Activation-Sparse and Low-Bit LLMs
candidates.abstract: Activation sparsity can reduce FFN weight traffic during single-user LLM decoding, but active channels must be identified early enough to avoid fetching unused weights. In pretrained SwiGLU models, training-free routing with the native gate performs substantially worse than routing with the up activation at high sparsity. We show that this ordering reverses after sparsity-aware training. Based on this insight, we introduce SGA-Sparse, which converts pretrained SwiGLU LLMs into fixed-budget activation-sparse models by training the existing gate projection directly as a top-k router. SGA-Sparse updates all model parameters end-to-end while preserving the original SwiGLU activation and introducing no auxiliary router parameters. After approximately 30B training tokens, LLaMA models from 1B to 8B achieve uniform per-token 75-85% FFN channel sparsity while remaining within 0.2-2.7 pp of their original dense checkpoints in average zero-shot accuracy. Because post-training quantization degrades sparsity-trained checkpoints, we further study two complementary quantization-aware training (QAT) recipes: continued-QAT largely recovers performance at 4-bit weight quantization, while joint-QAT performs better for the more aggressive sub-4-bit target. To compare activation sparsity with dense low-bit quantization, we translate the sparsity-induced reduction in weight traffic into an equivalent bit-width. Under this unified weight-traffic metric, our 2.5- and 1.5-bit-equivalent models establish a new accuracy-traffic Pareto frontier: the 2.5-bit-equivalent models match dense 3-bit QAT accuracy, while the 1.5-bit-equivalent models approach dense 2-bit models and outperform dense ternary models by 1.3 pp on average. These results establish native-gate training as a practical approach for combining high FFN sparsity with low-bit weights.
candidates.reason: 単一利用者デコードでFFN重み転送を減らす活性スパース化と低ビット化をSwiGLUゲート学習で実現する研究であり、LLMデコードの帯域律速へ直接取り組む。

candidates.title: STRIDE: Efficient Secure Transformer Inference via Inter-Operator Protocol and Operator Co-Design
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGOPS Annual Technical Conference
candidates.abstract: Secure inference based on homomorphic encryption (HE) and secure multi-party computation (MPC) protects both client inputs and model weights in GPT serving. Existing systems follow two paradigms: hybrid HE–MPC uses a type-driven heuristic that maps linear operators to HE and non-linear operators to MPC, while fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) executes entirely in the ciphertext domain to eliminate communication. Despite strong security guarantees, both remain inefficient in practice. Our profiling shows that the primary bottleneck lies in inter-operator overhead rather than individual operator inefficiency: type-driven protocol assignment and locally optimized layouts leave substantial switching and layout-transformation costs. Stride targets this overhead through two inter-operator optimizations: protocol assignment that accounts for operator affinity and switching cost, and attention refinement that improves HE affinity while preserving layout compatibility with interleaved encoding and offline–online alignment. Beyond these inter-operator optimizations, Stride further accelerates the resulting HE-heavy execution through optimized polynomial evaluation and dependency-driven multi-GPU scheduling. On GPT-2 and LLaMA-7B across three network settings, Stride achieves up to 3.83 × speedup over the faster of the two GPU-based baselines, Nexus and BLB, with one GPU per system. With four GPUs, Stride achieves up to 10.62 × speedup over the same single-GPU baselines.
candidates.reason: 同型暗号と秘密計算の演算子間プロトコルを共同設計しGPTサービングの秘匿推論を効率化するSTRIDEは、安全なTransformer推論システムへの直接貢献である。
